title: Rijiju Shares 'Dimagi Naxal' List After PM Modi's Independence Day Warning
excerpt: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju doubled down on PM Modi's I-Day remarks about 'dimagi naxals' by naming opposition leaders, prompting Congress leader P. Chidambaram to declare he is 'proud to be one.'
body:
• Union Minister Kiren Rijiju shared a list of people he described as 'dimagi naxals' after PM Modi used the term in his Independence Day speech to warn youth against ideological extremism.
  • Congress leader P. Chidambaram responded defiantly, saying he is 'proud to be a dimagi naxal,' turning the phrase into a badge of honour for the opposition.
  • PM Modi's speech from the Red Fort cautioned India's youth against those who spread ideological extremism — what he termed 'dimaagi naxals' — in a broader outreach to young voters.
  • The exchange has triggered a sharp political debate, with opposition parties calling the remarks an attempt to label dissent as extremism.

Modi's Independence Day Warning

Prime Minister Narendra Modi used his 80th Independence Day address from the Red Fort on August 15 to issue a pointed warning to India's youth about what he described as 'dimaagi naxals' — a term loosely translated as 'intellectual naxals' or those who spread ideological extremism through ideas rather than armed violence.

https://x.com/TimesNow/status/2088984183423283396

The remarks, part of a broader outreach to young Indians, cautioned against individuals and groups that Modi said attempt to mislead youth through distorted narratives and extremist ideologies. The speech framed the warning within the government's broader narrative about combating left-wing extremism, which Delhi has declared largely defeated in its armed form.

Rijiju Names Names

Union Minister Kiren Rijiju amplified the message by sharing what he described as a list of 'dimagi naxals' on social media, a move that drew immediate backlash from the opposition. Rijiju's post included references to Congress leaders and other opposition figures, escalating the political confrontation.

Rijiju maintained that the PM's remarks were not directed at opposition leaders specifically but at a broader ideological ecosystem. "He didn't call opposition leaders dimagi naxals," Rijiju said, according to the Times of India, while simultaneously circulating a list that the opposition interpreted as doing exactly that.

Chidambaram's Defiant Response

Senior Congress leader and former Union Minister P. Chidambaram responded with characteristic directness, declaring he was "proud to be one." The veteran politician's response quickly gained traction on social media, with opposition supporters adopting the 'dimagi naxal' label as a form of political defiance.

"Proud to be a dimagi Naxal."

— P. Chidambaram, Former Union Finance Minister

The Congress party has framed Modi's remarks as an attempt to equate political dissent with extremism, a charge the BJP has denied.

Political Context

The 'dimagi naxal' exchange follows a pattern of sharp rhetoric between the ruling BJP and the opposition. Modi has previously used terms like 'urban naxal' to describe what he sees as an intellectual ecosystem sympathetic to left-wing extremism. The Congress and other opposition parties have consistently rejected this framing as an attempt to delegitimise criticism.

The debate carries particular weight in 2026, with state elections on the horizon and both sides looking to energise their bases through identity-defining political battles.

What's Next

The fallout from Modi's Independence Day speech is likely to continue reverberating through Parliament and on social media. With Rijiju's list adding fuel to the fire, the 'dimagi naxal' debate has become the latest flashpoint in India's increasingly polarised political landscape. Opposition parties are expected to raise the issue when Parliament reconvenes.
